ruleSets.title: Rule sets
ruleSets.intro: A rule naming geosite: or geoip: needs a compiled list on disk. Nothing is downloaded until you ask, and the address below is the one that will be asked.
ruleSets.sourceHelp: $token is replaced with the tag being fetched. Clear the field to make downloading unavailable.
ruleSets.sourceInvalid: That does not look like an http or https address
ruleSets.noneNeededBody: Rules naming geosite: or geoip: are the ones that do. Plain domains and addresses work without anything downloaded.

deleteConfirm.title: Delete this list?
deleteConfirm.body: The rules that name it stay where they are and stop applying until it is downloaded again.

apps.title: Apps
apps.modeDisabledHint: Every app goes through the tunnel. The list below is kept but not applied.
apps.modeIncludeHint: Only the apps you tick go through the tunnel. Everything else goes out directly.
apps.modeExcludeHint: Every app goes through the tunnel except the ones you tick.
apps.selfHint: Always outside the tunnel: an app that fetched its own subscription through its own tunnel could never recover from a bad one.
apps.empty: This platform does not route by app
apps.emptyBody: Per-app routing is an Android feature. On the desktops every app uses the tunnel.
apps.nothingFoundBody: Try part of the name, or the package.
apps.hiddenBySystemBody: Everything matching this search is a system app, and those are hidden by the switch above.

dns.title: DNS
dns.remoteHint: Answers for names that go through the proxy, and is asked through it
dns.directHint: Answers for names that bypass the proxy
dns.footer: Two resolvers, always. One asked through the tunnel and one asked outside it is the whole reason a DNS query cannot say where you are; a single resolver for both is the classic leak.
dns.fakeIpHint: Answers from a private pool instead of resolving. Faster, and no real address reaches the system cache.
dns.independentCacheHint: One cache per resolver. Shared, two answers to the same name overwrite each other.

edit.label: Resolver
edit.help: Schemes: $schemes. A bare address means plain UDP. "local" hands the query to the system.
edit.unsupportedScheme: The core has no transport for that scheme
edit.missingAddress: There is no address after the scheme

qr.nodeCaption: Scan it in another client to add this server.

qr.subscriptionWarning: Anyone who scans this gets your subscription link, and with it every server on it. Show it only to a device you own.
qr.tooLong: This one is too long to scan. Copy the link instead.

silence.title: Silence on the wire
silence.body: Not one outgoing request you did not ask for. Below is the complete list of exceptions, and it is closed.
silence.blockListsMissing: on, but the list is not downloaded — open Rule sets
silence.footer: A fourth exception cannot appear without changing this screen.

identity.title: Device identifier
identity.sendHint: Only to your subscription's host. Panels that limit devices answer without it with a placeholder instead of servers. It is a random number for this install, not your phone's serial.
identity.resetHint: The panel will see a new device

connection.title: Connection
connection.killSwitchHint: Provided by Android: Always-on VPN with "Block connections without VPN". Tap to open it.
connection.killSwitchUnavailable: This system has no VPN settings screen
connection.hideUnavailableHint: Servers that did not answer a probe

routing.title: Routing

inactive.body: These rules are not in force right now: only Rules mode reads them.

routing.finalRuleHint: The last rule is always there and cannot be removed: routing must have a final outcome.

dropped.title: Some rules are not being applied
dropped.body: They name a rule set that is not on disk. The tunnel still comes up, but these rules do nothing until the sets are downloaded.

routing.emptyRules: No rules of your own yet
routing.emptyRulesBody: With no rules everything follows the final outcome. Add the first one to split the traffic.

diagnostics.title: Diagnostics
diagnostics.redactionNotice: UUIDs, passwords and subscription links are stripped automatically when copying and exporting.
diagnostics.logsEmptyBody: The core writes here while the tunnel runs. Connect and the lines will appear.
diagnostics.logsFilteredBody: No line passes the current level and search.
diagnostics.connectionsEmptyBody: This shows which rule matched each host. The list fills up while traffic flows.
diagnostics.configEmptyBody: The configuration appears the moment you connect: it is assembled from the chosen server, the rules and DNS.
diagnostics.configRedacted: Secrets are stripped. This is what goes to the core, minus the credentials.
diagnostics.statsEmptyBody: The chart shows the last 60 seconds; the rows below, this session's usage and the last week by day.
diagnostics.statsChart: Traffic over the last 60 seconds, peak $peak

exportWarning.title: Export the logs?
exportWarning.body: Credentials, subscription links and full addresses are stripped before saving. Read the file before sending it anywhere.

about.title: About
about.notAService: Commy is not a VPN service. No servers of ours, no bundled configs, no accounts and no backend.
about.storageDegraded: The database is not encrypted in this build. Secrets still live in the system keystore.
